title: SpecJudge comparison output
description: Payload emitted by `specjudge --json` and by specjudge.api.to_dict(). Version 1.1. Adding a field is a MINOR bump; removing one, changing its type, or changing what an existing value means is MAJOR. Obtain this file without cloning the repo: `specjudge --print-schema`.

schema_version.description: Version of this payload contract, independent of the specjudge package version.

data_state.description: How much the project told us. `scarce` also covers a judge that could not ground every dimension.

sources_read.description: Kinds of written source that contributed content, deduplicated, in discovery order: constitution, spec, tasks, plan, agents (AGENTS.md), claude (CLAUDE.md), cursor (.cursorrules), copilot (.github/copilot-instructions.md), adr. One entry per kind however many files of it were read. Open-ended: new source kinds are added in MINOR releases, so treat an unknown value as a source you do not recognise rather than as an error.

environment_only.description: True when every source read describes the repository (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) and none describes the work in progress. The result is then a floor — how demanding this codebase is to work in at all — not a recommendation for a specific piece of work.

judge_model.description: Local model used as the judge.

best_choice.description: model_id of the best-fitting model, or null when no model in the catalog is capable enough.

podium.description: Up to three model_ids by fit, gold first. Shorter when fewer models qualify, empty when none does.

demand.description: The judge's assessment of how demanding the project is, and the evidence behind it.

warnings.description: Human-readable warnings. Wording is not covered by the schema version.

evaluations.description: One entry per catalog model, ordered best fit first.

dimensions.description: Dimension name to demand level, or the literal `unsupported`. Dimension names and level vocabulary both come from data/rating-rules.yaml, so neither is enumerated here.

justification.description: The judge's own summary. Free text.

coverage.description: Human-readable grounding ratio. Free text; parse `evidence` instead.

evidence.description: Dimension name to the citation backing it.

status.description: grounded: the cited fragment exists and any quote matched. quote_unverified: fragment exists, quoted wording did not match. unsupported: the judge found nothing to cite.

fragment_id.description: Id of the cited project fragment. Null when the dimension is unsupported.

quote.description: Optional literal quote the judge offered alongside the id.

rating.description: Closed vocabulary fixed by the project constitution: changing it requires a constitutional amendment, not just a release.

justification.description: Why this model got this rating. Free text.

price_stale.description: True when the entry carries no pricing_date, so freshness cannot be verified. NOT a statement that the price is old.

pricing_date.description: ISO date the price was verified, or null when the catalog entry carries none.
